title: Writing Simple Sentences
introduction: Practise writing simple sentences with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: A simple sentence can tell who or what it is about and what happens or what it is like.
rules: Build a simple sentence with a subject and a verb. Add an object or description when needed.
Use a capital letter at the beginning, spaces between words and punctuation at the end.
Practise writing about different themes: school, food, family, animals, hobbies and weather.
Use and to join familiar words. Write short personal descriptions using a model. Use fictional details when practising online.

examples.question: Arrange: likes / Aina / mangoes.
steps: Start with the person, then the action and object.

examples.question: Arrange: can / jump / Rabbits.
steps: Use the base verb after can.

examples.question: Write a sentence about your schoolbag using has.
steps: Use has to describe a feature.

exercises.question: Put in order: swim / Fish
exercises.solution: Place the subject Fish before the verb swim; finish with a full stop.

exercises.question: Put in order: like / I / rice
exercises.solution: Start with I, then the verb like and the object rice.

exercises.question: Put in order: is / The cup / blue
exercises.solution: Place the subject first, then is and the adjective blue.

exercises.question: Put in order: jump / can / We
exercises.solution: Put We first, followed by can and the base verb jump.

exercises.question: Put in order: a kite / has / Ali
exercises.solution: Start with Ali, then has and the object a kite.

exercises.question: Put in order: are / The books / new
exercises.solution: Use the plural subject The books, then are and the adjective new.

exercises.question: Put in order: my / This is / bag
exercises.solution: Start with This is, then my and the noun bag.

exercises.question: Put in order: drinks / Mei / milk
exercises.solution: Put Mei first, then drinks and the object milk.

exercises.question: Put in order: play / They / football
exercises.solution: Start with They, followed by play and the object football.

exercises.question: Put in order: The dog / under the table / sleeps
exercises.answer: The dog sleeps under the table.
exercises.solution: Place the subject first, then sleeps and the phrase describing location.

exercises.question: Join: I like apples. I like bananas. Complete: I like apples ___ bananas.
exercises.solution: Use and to join two things you like without repeating the subject and verb.

exercises.question: Complete: My name ___ Aina.
exercises.solution: Use is with the singular subject My name.

exercises.question: Complete: I ___ seven years old.
exercises.solution: Use am with the subject I.

exercises.question: Complete: I have a red bag ___ a blue pen.
exercises.solution: Use and to join the two objects in the sentence.

summary: A simple sentence can tell who or what it is about and what happens or what it is like.
